Oakland Athletics (seed 22) vs Philadelphia Phillies (seed 11), home pattern 2-2-1-1-1, Game 1 at Citizens Bank Park in Philadelphia, and Oakland leads the series 1-0 with this win. Box score record: the three sources carry the linescore, the full batting and pitching lines, and a complete play log, and they agree on every printed number, with one run-accounting settlement (the Top 8 wild pitch run, below) and no other knot. The decisions are not printed; they are derived from the play log and the run charges on the card. Catfish Hunter takes the win: he left in the Bottom 6 with one out, runners at first and second, and a 5-3 lead, and the lead held the rest of the way (5.1 IP, 10 H, 3 ER, 0 BB, 3 SO, 2 HR). Steve Carlton takes the loss: he was charged with eight runs in 7.1 innings (10 H, 8 ER, 5 BB, 6 SO, 2 HR), five of them his own runners and three of them runners he left behind who scored behind Brad Lidge in the Top 8 (Steinbach on the wild pitch, Ellis on Chavez's double, and Murphy, who scored on Ellis's single off Carlton himself). No save: Dennis Eckersley closed the Bottom 9 with a six-run lead, 11-5, so no save arises. Run charges match the printed lines exactly: Philadelphia pitching allows 8 + 3 + 0 = 11 (Carlton eight, Lidge three, Papelbon none), and Oakland pitching allows 3 + 1 + 1 + 0 = 5 (Hunter three, Doolittle one, Hendriks one, Eckersley none). The charge detail: Carlton's eight are Murphy's Top 2 solo home run, four in the Top 5 (Henderson walked and scored on Jackson's single, Bando and Jackson singled and scored with McGwire on McGwire's 3-run home run), Murphy again in the Top 8 (walked and scored on Ellis's single, Carlton's last batter), Steinbach in the Top 8 (singled off Carlton and scored on Lidge's wild pitch, so the run stays Carlton's), and Ellis in the Top 8 (singled off Carlton and scored on Chavez's double behind Lidge). Lidge's three are Henderson in the Top 8 (Lidge hit him himself, and he scored on Chavez's double) and Tejada and Steinbach in the Top 9 (both reached off Lidge and scored on Ellis's double). Hunter's three are Callison in the Bottom 1 (singled and scored on Schmidt's double), Callison again in the Bottom 3 (solo home run), and Howard in the Bottom 4 (solo home run); Doolittle's one is Klein's Bottom 7 solo home run and Hendriks's one is Rollins's Bottom 8 solo home run. Printed RBI: Oakland 10 (McGwire 3, Ellis 3, Chavez 2, Jackson 1, Murphy 1) against 11 runs, the one run without an RBI being Steinbach's Top 8 run on Lidge's wild pitch (settlement below), and Philadelphia 5 (Callison 1, Klein 1, Schmidt 1, Howard 1, Rollins 1) against 5 runs, clean. The settlement: in the Top 8, after Ellis's single made it 6-4, Lidge relieved, hit Henderson to load the bases (Steinbach at third, Ellis at second, Henderson at first), and during Chavez's pinch-hit at-bat Lidge threw a wild pitch (the card prints WP: Brad Lidge 1) that scored Steinbach and moved Ellis and Henderson up; Chavez then doubled both of them home. That is why the printed batting line gives Chavez 2 RBI and not 3, why Oakland's printed RBI total is 10 for 11 runs, and why the play log's line on the double reads three runs in the inning sequence while only two of them ride on the double. The duplicate test ran before the number was assigned: the R1-11 series entry carried no stored games, so this box score is no duplicate, and this is the first game of the series in play order, booked as Game 1. The game: Philadelphia scored first in the Bottom 1 (Callison singled, Abreu moved him over, and Schmidt doubled him home), Murphy's solo home run tied it in the Top 2, and solo home runs by Callison in the Bottom 3 and Howard in the Bottom 4 put Philadelphia up 3-1. Oakland's Top 5 turned the game: Steinbach and Ellis went quietly, Henderson walked, Bando and Jackson singled (Jackson's drove Henderson home), and McGwire hit a 3-run home run for a 5-3 lead. Hunter left in the Bottom 6 with the bases filling, and Doolittle walked Rollins to load them before striking out Callison and getting Abreu to line out, stranding three. Klein's home run in the Bottom 7 cut it to 5-4. The Top 8 broke it open: Tejada grounded out, Murphy walked, Steinbach and Ellis singled (Ellis's scored Murphy, the last batter Carlton faced), Lidge came in and hit Henderson, threw the wild pitch that scored Steinbach, and gave up Chavez's two-run double for a 9-4 lead. Rollins homered in the Bottom 8 to make it 9-5. In the Top 9, Canseco struck out, Tejada singled, Murphy flied out, Steinbach walked, and Ellis doubled both runners home off Lidge; Papelbon struck out Henderson to end the inning at 11-5. Eckersley pitched a scoreless Bottom 9 (Klein singled and stole second behind him, stranded at third). Philadelphia out-hit Oakland 14 to 13 and stranded 10 runners, including the bases loaded in the Bottom 6. Home runs: Oakland two (Murphy, McGwire) and Philadelphia four (Callison, Howard, Klein, Rollins). Doubles: Ellis and Chavez for Oakland and Schmidt and Howard for Philadelphia; no triples. Errors: none by either club. Hit batters: one, Henderson, hit by Lidge in the Top 8 (the card prints HBP by: Brad Lidge 1); the scorecard grids print an HBP column for every pitcher on both clubs, so HB is carried card-sourced for all seven pitchers (Lidge 1, the other six 0) and the hit batter check runs on real data. Wild pitch: Lidge 1, printed, the Top 8 run described above. Sacrifices: Schmidt's Bottom 3 sacrifice bunt is the game's only sacrifice of either kind, so the split lines read SH 1 for Schmidt and SH 0 and SF 0 for every other batter, log-proven. Stolen bases, as printed: Klein 2 (Bottom 3 and Bottom 9); Manuel's other graded steal send in the Bottom 9 was a held runner who did not get a good jump, not an attempt. Caught stealing: none. Double plays grounded into, counted from the play log: one, Ellis in the Top 6 (a 3-4-3 double play that erased the threat after the Murphy and Steinbach singles). Substitutions: Oakland made one, Eric Chavez pinch-hit for Sal Bando in the Top 8 and stayed in at third base, doubling home two runs (1 for 1); Bando himself had walked in the Top 7, before the change. Philadelphia made no substitution of any kind. Batters faced are counted from the play log and tie to the batting PA totals both ways (Oakland 46 PA against 46 Philadelphia BF: Carlton 36, Lidge 9, Papelbon 1; Philadelphia 42 PA against 42 Oakland BF: Hunter 26, Doolittle 7, Hendriks 5, Eckersley 4). Oakland PA is AB 39 plus BB 6 plus Henderson's hit by pitch; Philadelphia PA is AB 40 plus BB 1 plus Schmidt's sacrifice bunt. Nine decisions were graded. Dick Williams made 4 (2 paid off, 0 backfired, 2 neutral): the Bottom 6 pitching change to Sean Doolittle paid off at +0.63, the game's signature call, walking the bases loaded and then escaping with no runs; the Top 8 pinch hitter Chavez paid off at +1.71, the game's best single grade; the Bottom 8 pitching change to Liam Hendriks was neutral at -0.27 (Rollins homered behind it) and the Bottom 9 change to Dennis Eckersley neutral at +0.23. Charlie Manuel made 5 (1 paid off, 2 backfired, 2 neutral): the Top 9 pitching change to Jonathan Papelbon paid off at +0.57; the Top 8 pitching change to Brad Lidge backfired at -2.37, the game's worst single grade (hit batter, wild pitch run, and a two-run double behind it); the Bottom 9 steal send backfired at -0.86 (Klein held); and two steal sends were neutral at -0.26 each (Bottom 3 and Bottom 9, Klein safe both times). Managers: Dick Williams (Oakland) and Charlie Manuel (Philadelphia). Venue is Citizens Bank Park. Game 2 availability, under the house convention that reads only this game: Hunter (16 outs) and Carlton (22 outs) are both UNAVAILABLE, and Doolittle (5 outs), Lidge (4), Hendriks (3), Eckersley (3) and Papelbon (1) are all free. Both clubs started their rotation number 1, Hunter for Oakland and Carlton for Philadelphia, and the rotations turn to the number 2 starters for Game 2 regardless.

Oakland Athletics (seed 22) vs Philadelphia Phillies (seed 11), home pattern 2-2-1-1-1, Game 2 at Citizens Bank Park in Philadelphia, and Oakland leads the series 2-0 with this win. The decisions are not printed; they are derived from the play log and the run charges on the card. Andrew Bailey takes the win, a scorer's choice: starter Vida Blue pitched only 4.0 innings and faced one batter in the Bottom 5, Klein, whose leadoff home run was Blue's sixth run charged, so at under five innings Blue cannot take the win; Liam Hendriks relieved and recorded no outs, allowing Schmidt's single and Harper's 2-run home run; Bailey then retired Howard, Utley and Ruiz in order, two of them on strikes, for a scoreless Bottom 5 with Oakland ahead 13-8, and the lead never changed hands again (Oakland led from the Top 1 onward and Philadelphia never tied it after the Top 5). Robin Roberts takes the loss: the runs that put Oakland ahead to stay came off him in the Top 1, Philadelphia trailed 6-5 when his work ended after the Top 4, and the Phillies never tied or led again, even though Ranger Suarez gave up the seven-run Top 5 behind him. No save: Dennis Eckersley closed the Bottom 9 with a four-run lead, 15-11. Run charges match the printed lines exactly: Philadelphia pitching allows 6 + 7 + 0 + 1 + 1 = 15 (Roberts six, Suarez seven, Reed none, Lidge one, Papelbon one), and Oakland pitching allows 6 + 2 + 0 + 0 + 2 + 1 + 0 = 11 (Blue six, Hendriks two, Bailey none, Doolittle none, Fingers two, Honeycutt one, Eckersley none). The charge detail: Roberts's six are the three in the Top 1 (Henderson unearned, below; Bando and Canseco earned on Canseco's 2-run home run), Canseco again in the Top 3 (doubled and scored on Tejada's single), and two unearned runs in the Top 4 (Henderson on Rollins's error, below; Bando, who scored on McGwire's single after the error should have ended the inning), which is why his printed line reads 6 R and only 3 ER. Suarez's seven are the entire seven-run Top 5, every run charged to him: Canseco (walked, scored on Steinbach's single), Tejada (singled, scored on Ellis's single), Steinbach and Ellis (singled, scored on Jackson's single), and Henderson, Jackson and McGwire on McGwire's 3-run home run. Lidge's one is Canseco in the Top 8 (doubled, scored on Murphy's single) and Papelbon's one is Chavez's Top 9 pinch-hit home run. Blue's six are the five in the Bottom 4 (Schmidt on Utley's double, Howard and Utley on Rollins's single, Rollins and Callison on Callison's 2-run home run) and Klein's Bottom 5 leadoff home run, the one batter Blue faced in the fifth. Hendriks's two are Schmidt and Harper in the Bottom 5 (singled, then scored with Harper on Harper's 2-run home run). Fingers's two are Schmidt and Harper in the Bottom 7, Schmidt unearned (below) and Harper earned on his second home run. Honeycutt's one is Ruiz in the Bottom 8. Printed RBI: Oakland 13 (McGwire 4, Canseco 2, Jackson 2, Tejada 1, Murphy 1, Steinbach 1, Ellis 1, Chavez 1) against 15 runs, the two runs without an RBI both being Henderson's error runs, settled below; and Philadelphia 10 (Harper 4, Callison 2, Rollins 2, Klein 1, Utley 1) against 11 runs, the one run without an RBI being Ruiz's Bottom 8 run, settled below. The settlements: in the Top 1, Henderson singled and stole second, and Bando's single plus Schmidt's error at third (batter to second) scored him; the scorer charged no RBI on the play, so Henderson's run is unearned and carries no RBI, while the two runs on Canseco's home run behind it are earned. In the Top 4, Steinbach walked, Ellis flied out, and Henderson forced Steinbach at second; Bando singled Henderson to third, Jackson reached on Rollins's error at short and Henderson scored on the play (unearned, no RBI), and McGwire's single scored Bando (unearned, coming after what should have been the third out). In the Bottom 7, Schmidt reached on Chavez's 2-base error at third and scored on Harper's home run: the run is unearned on Fingers's line but carries Harper's RBI, as a home run run does. In the Bottom 8, Ruiz doubled, Rollins bunted him to third, and he scored on Honeycutt's wild pitch during Callison's strikeout (the card prints WP: Rick Honeycutt 1), which is why Philadelphia's printed RBI total is 10 for 11 runs.
